faq: Can you promise more paid installs?
No. Results depend on your app, pricing and traffic. We remove friction we can see, add tracking so you can measure it and report honestly on what the numbers show.
Do you work with the pricing plans in my Dev Center?
Yes. We review the plans you have, suggest clearer names and limits, and update the screens that show them. Changes to the plans themselves are made by you or in your account with your approval.
Can you ask site owners for reviews?
Only in ways Wix allows. We add one polite prompt after a good moment and never offer rewards or filter who is asked. Reviews must come from real site owners.
What do you track events with?
Whatever you already use, such as Google Analytics, Mixpanel or PostHog. With nothing in place, we suggest a free option and set up events for the steps that matter.
desc:
Wix app conversion and onboarding work turns installs into active, paying sites. Ecom Swift LLC walks through your app as a new site owner, finds where people give up, and fixes the first-run flow, plan wording and upgrade prompts.

## Why do Wix app installs not turn into active users?

Most installs stall in the first few minutes. The site owner opens the dashboard, sees a blank screen or a long form, does not know what to do first, and leaves. The app stays installed but unused, and a few weeks later it is removed or never paid for. The cause is rarely the idea. It is usually the path between install and the first moment the owner sees value.

## How onboarding and plans affect revenue

Active use comes before payment. A site owner who has completed setup and seen the widget on their page has a reason to keep the app and to upgrade when they hit a limit. An owner who never finished setup has no reason to pay.

Plans work the same way. If plan names are vague or limits are hidden, owners cannot tell which tier fits them, so they pick none. If the upgrade prompt appears at a random moment, it feels like a sales pitch. If it appears exactly when a limit is reached, it feels like help. Clear steps and honest wording tend to improve activation and upgrades, though results depend on your app, your audience and your pricing, so we do not promise a figure.

## What a strong first-run experience includes

- A first dashboard screen that says what the app does and shows the single next step.
- A setup checklist that tracks progress and remembers where the owner stopped.
- Short, specific button labels instead of generic ones.
- Plan names and limits written in plain terms, with the differences side by side.
- An upgrade prompt that appears when a plan limit is reached, not before.
- Honest trial wording with no hidden conditions.
- Event tracking on key steps, so you can see where owners drop out.
- A welcome email that explains the first action to take.
- A cancel path that is easy to find, which builds trust and gives feedback.

## How we work on your conversion

We install your app on a fresh test site and go through it as a stranger. We note every point of confusion, then group the notes into fixes by effort and likely effect. After agreeing the list with you, we make the changes in your repository.

The Basic package covers the walk-through, a clearer first screen and a few wording or button fixes. Standard adds a setup checklist, rebuilt plan comparison text, a limit-reached prompt and tracking on key steps. Premium adds a fuller onboarding sequence, a review of trial and plan limits, a written welcome email, one A/B test and handover notes. We follow Wix App Market rules for pricing and for how reviews may be requested.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us the numbers you already track, even if they are rough.
- Let us try the app from a brand new account.
- Keep plan names short and descriptive.
- Ask for reviews only in ways Wix allows.

**Avoid:**
- Adding more steps to onboarding. Fewer, clearer steps usually work better.
- Pushing upgrades before the owner has seen value.
- Offering incentives for reviews, which breaks App Market rules.
- Changing many things at once, because you will not know which change helped.

## Who this is for

An app owner with plenty of installs but few paying sites. A developer who built a strong feature and never designed the first five minutes. A founder preparing to introduce paid plans who wants the wording right the first time.

## What we need from you

Access as a collaborator to your repository and Dev Center, a test site or permission to make one, and a short note on your current plans and what you track. We never need your password. If you have analytics events already, send the list, and we will build on it.

Once the changes are live, you can add a cancel survey, extra A/B tests or in-app tips as separate add-ons.
